gen-dafont-bloody-gf-stack-sans-headline: Bloody's big round bowls give it a blunt, dripping-loud presence, with little swelling or thinning in the line. Stack Sans Headline follows in sans, wide-gapped and crisp.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-stack-sans-notch: Bloody's low-contrast, big round bowls make the heading hit hard and fast. Stack Sans Notch carries the longer text in sans-serif with open curves and rod-like strokes, so words feel full-bodied and easy to enter.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-stack-sans-text: Bloody leads with commanding, big round lowercase bowls, while Stack Sans Text drops beneath it in a plain sans with a marker-like constant line. Long text feels smooth and uniform.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-sulphur-point: Sulphur Point is a plain sans with a marker-like line and clear gaps in its a, c, e and s. Over a long stretch it reads steadily and sturdily, and Bloody's big round heading bowls loom above it.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-tiktok-sans: Modern and brisk, with lowercase that rises nearly to cap height, the type here feels tall and wide-open. TikTok Sans keeps a longer passage moving smoothly beneath Bloody's heavy, round heading.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-ubuntu-sans: Bloody brings commanding, big round bowls to the top, with a bloody weight and low contrast. Ubuntu Sans has tubular, bent-pipe strokes, and the shared roundness is what ties them.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-vend-sans: Commanding and loud, Bloody rounds out its lowercase into big bowls. Vend Sans answers in plain sans with ruler-straight, constant-width strokes, and both look cut from one gauge of tubing, which is what joins them.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-yaldevi: Loud and round, Bloody shows off its commanding, big-bowled lowercase, with Yaldevi underneath in a plain sans with outsized lowercase proportions. Its e opens clearly to the right.
gen-dafont-brusher-fs-amulya: Romantic and brushy, Brusher flows in a calligraphic hand with a quiet, level beat. Amulya's generous, open curves in sans give a modern counterweight, and that gap between them is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-brusher-fs-plein: Brusher writes in a calligraphic hand, its cord-like curves as heavy as its stems and its e wide open. Plein sits beside it as a plain sans with clear channels into each round letter, and it feels best for brief lines.
